chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Ellington versus McKinney's Cotton Pickers
summary: He says Ellington always sounded the same but the Cotton Pickers were jumping when he heard them in Cleveland.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them

SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTE
J. C. HIGGINBOTHAM
Side 1, Reels 13 & 14
How did Duke Ellington's band compare to, say, the Cotton Pickers in popularity?
I don't like to talk about those things.
I mean as far as the general public was concerned.
Well, here's the only answer I can give you. McKinney's Cotton Picks They had a band. They had a band! But, every time I go to hear Duke, I hear the same thing. Practically the same thing.

... no, he's a great musician. He's one of the greatest musicians. But, when you said the Cotton Pickers, the band was jumping then. The first time I heard them was in Cleveland, Ohio and what a band. Yeah, ... you don't know about that, you weren't even (born--)
